description: Guide a student to diagnose overfitting in a 12-parameter trading strategy that performs well in-sample (2020-2022) but poorly out-of-sample (2023-2024). This is a conceptual diagnosis task — no single-line fix exists.

student_openings.beginner_no_finance: I spent weeks tuning my trading strategy with 12 parameters and it has an amazing Sharpe ratio on the training data! But when I test it on new data, the performance drops a lot. Is there a bug somewhere?
student_openings.intermediate_developer: My multi-indicator strategy (12 parameters) shows a big Sharpe ratio decay between training (2020-2022) and test (2023-2024) periods. I've verified the code is correct — no bugs. What's happening?
student_openings.advanced_quant: I'm seeing classic in-sample/out-of-sample degradation in my 12-parameter strategy. The Sharpe drops significantly. I suspect I've over-specified the model but I'd like help diagnosing the degrees-of-freedom issue and identifying remedies.

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Student understands that the strategy is overfitting to the training data due to excessive parameter count, identifies the Sharpe decay as evidence, and proposes remedies like reducing parameters, cross-validation, or walk-forward testing.
required_capabilities: Run the strategy and observe train vs test performance
Identify the Sharpe ratio decay between periods
Diagnose overfitting as the root cause
Note the excessive number of parameters (12)
